title: BLF Human Review Practice Items
purpose: Interface calibration examples for native evaluators prior to analytical pilot evaluation.
usage_rule: Practice items teach interface mechanics only and are strictly excluded from Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA) and Gold dataset promotion.

items.context: Neutral description of morning daybreak in standard everyday speech.
items.intended_meaning: The sun rises in the morning.
items.interface_concept_taught: Multiple candidates can both be acceptable; rate candidates independently; choose preferred candidate(s).
items.facilitator_notes: Candidate A is common standard. Candidate B has literary lexical choice. Reviewers should rate both independently without feeling compelled to mark one bad if both are valid.

items.context: Simple description of bird behavior in nature.
items.intended_meaning: The bird flies in the sky.
items.interface_concept_taught: Rating unacceptable candidates as UNGRAMMATICAL or MEANING_DIFFERS; selecting preferred candidate [A]; offering optional correction if needed.
items.facilitator_notes: Candidate A is natural standard. Candidate B violates semantic selection (MEANING_DIFFERS / UNNATURAL). Candidate C lacks locative case marking (UNGRAMMATICAL).

items.context: An isolated utterance without prior conversational context.
items.interface_concept_taught: Using NEEDS_CONTEXT or MEANING_DIFFERS when meaning or acceptability depends on unstated conversational context or person agreement.
items.facilitator_notes: Candidate B matches 3rd person 'he/she came yesterday'. Candidate A has 1st person inflection 'I came yesterday'. If intended meaning is not matched, rater can use MEANING_DIFFERS or note NEEDS_CONTEXT.
